title: Build a roster dispatch can use

scenes.title: Build a roster dispatch can use
scenes.narration: Welcome to Resgrid Academy. In this lesson, we will build a roster dispatch can use. An out-of-date roster leaves dispatchers guessing which station, team, or role a member belongs to. We will explain the features, the setup decisions, and a practical way to check the result.

scenes.title: A department scenario
scenes.narration: A volunteer department creates Station 1 and Station 2 groups, invites 24 members and assigns Engineer and Firefighter roles. Dispatch, notifications, permissions and reports all start from who belongs to which group, so set this up first. The examples in this series use a fictional department and are teaching scenarios, not default settings.

scenes.title: Personnel
scenes.narration: Personnel. Member accounts, contact details and status. Invite members or add them directly, then check that each has a mobile number or email address.

scenes.title: Manage Invites
scenes.narration: Manage Invites. Email invitations for new members to join the department. Send invitations and follow up on any that have not been accepted.

scenes.title: Groups & Stations
scenes.narration: Groups & Stations. Stations and groups that organize members and units. Create a station group for each station with its address, and organizational groups for teams, then add members.

scenes.title: Personnel roles
scenes.narration: Personnel roles. Roles such as Firefighter, EMT or Officer. Create the roles you dispatch or report on, and assign them to members.

scenes.title: Add Person
scenes.narration: Add Person. Create a member account directly instead of sending an invitation. Have your member list with email addresses or mobile numbers, and decide how stations or teams are grouped.

scenes.title: New Group
scenes.narration: New Group. Create a station or group. Have your member list with email addresses or mobile numbers, and decide how stations or teams are grouped.

scenes.title: Configure one useful workflow
scenes.narration: For the training scenario, work in this order. Step 1. Create Station 1 and Station 2 with their addresses. Step 2. Invite sample members and assign their station groups. Step 3. Create Engineer and Officer roles and assign them deliberately.

scenes.title: Verify the result
scenes.narration: Now verify the result. Verify a sample member appears in the correct group and role. Check an accepted invitation and the member contact details. A common problem to watch for: An invitation is not an accepted membership. A role label is not proof of a current certification. Review both separately.

scenes.title: Try it with your department
scenes.narration: Your practice task is simple. Invite one sample member, assign a station and role, and have that member sign in. Track unaccepted invitations. Record the result, who owns the follow-up, and when it should be reviewed. Use the linked feature scripts for the detailed screen recording plan.
